task.description: Validate src/design/iss0620-gbl134-per-tenant-forward-fix.md and the migration it specifies, migrations/GBL-137_iss0620_recreate_per_tenant_shadows.sql, for GH-573/ISS-0620 (BLOCKER -- a 4-table misclassification in GBL-134 that already executed a destructive DROP against tenant_default in 2 databases with no guard). This migration lineage (GBL-134/135/136) has a documented history of 2 prior classification errors -- apply extra scrutiny. GBL-137 is purely additive (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS / CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS only, no DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE) recreating tenant_default copies of 4 tables (artifact_activation_groups, entity_definitions, entity_record_latest, entity_type_instances) that GBL-134 wrongly dropped. result.summary: Independently re-verified all 9 acceptance criteria for GBL-137/ISS-0620's forward-fix. 8 of 9 PASS with strong evidence; 1 FAILS the explicit acceptance criterion 'lint_design_artefact.py exits 0 with no BLOCKER/MAJOR'. Verified items: (1) Schema fidelity -- read GBL-137, migrations/094_entity_subsystem.sql, and migrations/046_repository_activations.sql in full; every column name/type/default/constraint/index for all 4 tables (entity_definitions, entity_type_instances, entity_record_latest, artifact_activation_groups) matches exactly, confirmed additionally by live \d inspection of bpm_test AND bpm_dev post-migration -- byte-for-byte match. (2) FK check -- ran own grep for REFERENCES clauses against all 4 table names across src/ and migrations/: zero matches, confirming no FK dependents. (3) Idempotency -- read the DO $$ block in full; pg_namespace existence guard is correct (skips schemas that don't exist, does not error); ran 'zig build migrate' against bpm_test live and confirmed GBL-137 shows 'skip' (already applied, genuine no-op) -- 'No new migrations to apply.' Independently confirmed via docker exec psql that bpm_dev (previously missing all 4 tables per the design doc's own scope note) now has entity_definitions with the correct shape, and bpm_test (previously already had empty shells from an unrelated reprovisioning event) is unchanged -- both database states behave correctly. (4) GBL-134 header-only correction -- ran git diff against main: the change is purely additive comment lines (lines 34-56), zero bytes of the executable DO $$ body changed. (5) No destructive statement -- grep for DROP/TRUNCATE/DELETE in GBL-137 returns only comment-text and the 'deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ' column name (false-positive substring match, not a statement); confirmed zero executable destructive statements. (6) Lint allow-list scoping -- git diff on tools/lint_dual_schema_table_names.py shows exactly the 4 expected names added with a clear comment marking them KNOWN/INTENTIONAL/TEMPORARY pending a separately-reviewed follow-up migration, matching the GBL-136/artifact_versions precedent pattern. (7) Non-local/production exposure -- ran own grep for DATABASE_URL/production/deploy/cloud-provider hostnames across docker-compose*.yml and .github/workflows/*.yml: zero matches, confirming ISSUE-FIXER's claim. (8) ISS-0623/GH-580 scope check -- confirmed docs/issues/ISS-0623.json exists as its own MAJOR-severity issue (not folded into ISS-0620), filed on GitHub (#580), and present in handoffs/global_queue.json with status QUEUED -- correctly deferred, not bundled. FAILING ITEM (9): ran 'python tools/lint_design_artefact.py src/design/iss0620-gbl134-per-tenant-forward-fix.md' via .venv/Scripts/python.exe -- exit 1, 2 MAJOR findings (E010: missing 'Public interface' section, missing 'Error taxonomy' section) plus 3 MINOR schema-qualified-name findings. This is not a false positive or a template mismatch: the direct lineage precedent for this exact artefact class, src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md (the GBL-136 forward-fix design for the SAME GBL-134 migration, same migration-only/no-Zig-functions shape), passes this same linter with exit 0 BLOCKER=0 MAJOR=0 MINOR=4 because it includes '## 2. Public interface -- new migration: GBL-136' and '## 3. Error taxonomy / cross-table FK ordering' sections adapted to a migration-only design (interface = the migration itself and its guard behavior; errors = exception-handling/skip conditions the DO block encounters). ISS-0620's design doc has no equivalent headings anywhere -- it has the content (idempotency guard behavior in Safety Properties #2, the 'no recovery path found' condition in §2) but never under a section the linter's REQUIRED_E_HEADINGS regex recognizes. Per CLAUDE.md's own Completeness checklist ('All public function signatures are listed', 'All error cases are named in an error taxonomy section') and this run's own acceptance criteria, this is a real gap, correctable in minutes by renaming/adding two headings around existing content -- not a reason to rewrite the design.

issues.description: src/design/iss0620-gbl134-per-tenant-forward-fix.md is missing a 'Public interface' (or 'Interface'/'API') section, per lint_design_artefact.py E010. Fix: add a section (e.g. '## Public interface — new migration: GBL-137') identifying GBL-137 itself as the interface surface: its filename, that it takes no parameters, runs as a public-pass GBL migration, and its externally-observable effect (idempotent per-tenant CREATE TABLE/CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS for 4 named tables). Follow the exact pattern already used in src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md section 2.

src/design/iss0620-gbl134-per-tenant-forward-fix.md is missing an 'Error taxonomy' (or 'Errors'/'Error cases') section, per lint_design_artefact.py E010. The content already exists but is scattered (Safety Properties #2's schema-exists guard/skip behavior, section 2's 'no recovery path found — no WAL archiving, no backup' finding) -- it needs to be consolidated under a heading the linter recognizes, naming the cases explicitly: (a) tenant row exists but schema does not -> skipped cleanly via pg_namespace check, not an error; (b) table already exists in target schema -> CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is a safe no-op; (c) pre-drop data loss -> not recoverable, no error to raise, documented as a known irreversible condition rather than a live error path. Follow the pattern in src/design/iss0617-gbl134-missing-tables-followup.md section 3.

3 MINOR schema-qualified-name findings in the design doc prose (lines 95, 105, 127: public.entity_definitions, public.tenant, information_schema.tables) per lint_design_artefact.py E030. These are prose references describing already-qualified system catalog/table names accurately and do not block PASS, but CODE-DESIGNER should consider using unqualified names in prose per the anti-patterns.md convention when revising for ISS-VALIDATOR-01/02.
